author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Several merchant vessels in the northern Gulf and Gulf of Oman were hit by disabling fires during overnight military activity, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported Wednesday.

The British navy-affiliated agency said it could not initially confirm casualties or environmental damage. In a separate incident about 24 nautical miles from Port Rashid in the United Arab Emirates, UKMTO reported a vessel listing at anchor, possibly after taking on water following an attack by an unknown projectile.

The incidents came after U.S. Central Command said it destroyed five Iranian crude tankers following attempted missile attacks on a U.S. Navy warship. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards then claimed attacks on two U.S. vessels and eight oil tankers. Those claims remained attributed statements in the early reporting, not independently confirmed findings.

The situation is developing, and basic facts may change as crews, ship operators and maritime authorities report damage. Confirmed casualty numbers, pollution effects, vessel identities and consequences for commercial traffic were not available in the initial account. Shipping advisories and official notices will be the key sources for operational updates.
dek: A British maritime agency reported several ships disabled during overnight military activity, with casualties and environmental effects not yet confirmed.
headline: Merchant vessels disabled by fires in Gulf and Gulf of Oman
